Shri K.S. Baghel - Government Advocate for the respond Heard on I.A. No.8788/2024, which is first application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail filed on behalf of appellant Sonu arising out of judgment dated 02.11.2023 delivered in SC No.56/2020 by Special Judge, Exclusive Special Court, POCSO Act, 2012.

entities.text: Special Judge, Exclusive Special Court, POCSO Act, 2012
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The appellant has been convicted under Sections 5(L)/6, 5(J)(II)/6 of POCSO Act R/w Sections 376(3), 376(2)(N), 376(2)(M) of IPC and sentenced to undergo R.I for 20 years with fine of Rs.5,000/- and under Section 363 of IPC and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 3 years with fine of Rs.2,000/- with default stipulations.

Learned counsel for the appellant submits that though the appellant has spent about one and half years of actual jail custody and even the DNA report is in matching configuration, but the age of the victim has not been properly assessed by the Court.

It is stated that the victim (PW/1) herself has admitted that she has willingly married the present appellant and the child has been born out of the said relationship, who was one and half years of age as on 24.08.2021.

It is further admitted by 2 CRA-335-2024 the victim in her deposition that presently she is 21 years of age which as per the appellant will translate to the victim having attained the age of majority on the date of occurrence.

Even PW/2 father of victim has deposed that the victim has married the present appellant out of her own wish and at present, she is between 20-22 years of age and she is living happily with the present appellant, who is son-in-law of this witness PW/2.

On the aspect of age determination, apart from admission of victim and her father, it is contended that the Head Master (PW/5) has stated that there is no source information on the basis of which the date of birth has been entered in the school register and, therefore, the determination of age is on debatable note, though subject to final adjudication of this Court in appeal.
The learned counsel for State on his part has vehemently opposed the application for suspension of sentence on the basis of written objection.
It is not disputed that the pendency of the present application has been intimated to the victim party.
Considering the aforesaid, but without any conclusive opinion on the merits of the case, the application for suspension of sentence is allowed.
